subject: general
question: Where does the cash grants in aid from foreign countries are classified?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Non-tax revenue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cash grants in aid from foreign countries** are classified as **non-tax revenue**.
 
• Non-tax revenue includes all revenue that the government receives other than taxes.
 
• Examples of non-tax revenue include grants, fees, fines, and dividends from public sector enterprises.
 
• Cash grants are typically given by foreign countries to support various sectors such as education, health, infrastructure, and disaster relief.
 
• Non-tax revenue is crucial for the government as it provides additional funds for public expenditure without imposing taxes on citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Expenditure:**

 
 
• Refers to the expenses incurred for the day-to-day functioning of the government and maintenance of infrastructure.
 
• Includes salaries, pensions, interest payments, and subsidies.
 
• Does not result in the creation of assets.
 
 
 
• **Capital Receipts:**
 
 
• Include loans, disinvestment, and other receipts that create liabilities or reduce assets.
 
• Are used for capital expenditure which leads to asset creation.
 
 
 
• **Tax Revenue:**
 
 
• Comprises taxes collected by the government such as income tax, GST, customs duty, and excise duty.
 
• It is the primary source of revenue for the government.
 
 
 
• **Non-tax Revenue Sources:**
 
 
• Interest receipts, dividends, and profits from public sector enterprises.
 
• Fees and fines collected by various government departments.
 
• Grants and donations from foreign countries and international organizations.
